parsed.faithful: The persons who had the liberty of voting were such Roman citizens as belonged to the curia, or actually lived in the city, and conformed to the customs and rites of their proper curia; and all were excluded who dwelt without the bounds of the city, or retained the ceremonies of their own country, even although they had been honoured with the jus civitatis. (See CRIZENS.) The place where the curia met was the comitium, a part of the forum. No fixed time was appointed for holding any of the comitia, but they were convened as business required.
